title: Natives urge full inquiry; Coroner's inquest into 2 deaths should be broadened: Families
article: The families of two First Nations men killed in a jailhouse fire almost three years ago want a coroner's inquest to shed light on the wide-sweeping issues facing people in native communities.
Ricardo Wesley and James Goodwin, both 20, burned to death in a police lockup on Jan. 8, 2006 at the Kashechewan First Nation police station in Ontario's far north, on the shore of James Bay.

Coroner's inquests are mandatory when there is a death in police custody and the inquiry was originally expected to take a wide view of the issues surrounding the death of the two men. But Wesley family lawyer Julian Falconer said in Toronto yesterday the guidelines were rewritten when the presiding coroner changed.

A scheduled three-month hearing was shortened to two weeks when Regional Coroner Dr. David Eden took control of the case and the focus was narrowed to exclude broader issues, including the funding and training for First Nations police, Falconer said.
While the inquest is scheduled to start in Cochrane next month, lawyers are hashing out some preliminary issues at a hearing in Toronto, which continues today.

"The Wesley family takes the position a grave injustice has occurred," Falconer said outside the Grosvenor St. coroner's court. "They were given the assurance that a broad-ranging inquiry into numerous complex and difficult systemic issues would occur."

Falconer and co-counsel Kimberly Murray would also like to see the inquest moved from Cochrane to a larger media centre like Ottawa so the public would have a better opportunity to learn about those issues.
The Deputy Grand Chief of the Nishnawbe Aski Nation said he would welcome an opportunity to examine the problems facing the remote community.

"There are problems people need to see if they are ever going to be fixed," Alvin Fiddler said outside the hearing. "They are long-term problems that are easier to ignore because they are so far away."

Buildings were allowed to burn to the ground in Kashechewan because the only fire truck was abandoned after it became too hard to start. The police jail was also rundown and the men died after an officer could not get the padlock on the cell to open.
The fire apparently started in the cell and people could hear the men's screams as they were engulfed in flames.
